text:
maya: Brain dump from today's sync: proposing a 'commit ladder' that combines baseline reserved GPUs + time-limited burst credits + an onboarding prewarm. want product + infra tradeoffs before i write the RFC.
ben: can you capture the customer-visible promises? sales needs plain bullets we can hand to procurement.
lina: yes, simple mapping please. procurement hates surprises. examples with monthly math.
maya: customer promises draft: 1) baseline capacity guaranteed (X GPUs) 2) burst credits for transient peaks (consumed before overage billing) 3) 48h soft-proration on step changes 4) one-time prewarm on upgrade (opt-in) 5) transparent fallback to shared pool with degraded variant.
sam: infra: how are burst credits accounted? token-based counter per-tenant? what about cross-region usage?
ben: implementation idea: burst_credits expressed in "gpu-minutes" or tokenized milliseconds of CPU/GPU time. track per-region ledger; allow borrow across regions with penalty or deny if cross-region disabled.
ravi: ops ask: how do we surface when a tenant is burning burst vs hitting baseline? need Console UX + tracing.
jess: pilot ask: can we offer a temporary trial top-up of burst to exercise production traffic? customers want to test peak behavior.
maya: yes, pilot flow: grant +50% burst for 7 days, monitor telemetry. billing: no overage during trial.
ben: API surfaces: tenant config fields: commit_tier, baseline_gpus, burst_credit, prewarm_enabled. sample: ```json {\"commit_tier\":\"tier-B\", \"baseline_gpus\":30, \"burst_credit_minutes\":43200, \"prewarm_enabled\":true} ```
sam: autoscale policy: allow instantaneous scale-up while within burst credit. when burst exhausted, enforce baseline + queue/route to shared. downscale cooldown 10m by default, adjustable per-tenant.
lina: refund/step-down policy: customers request a 7-day notice window for step-downs to avoid billing churn. ok to have soft-proration but no refunds unless explicit SLA breach.
ben: engineering constraints: routing fallback must include model-variant degeneracy; we need contract between serving runtime and router to accept "degrade_to_variant" hints. also need migration to add fields to tenant DB. estimate 3 sprints for core work.
ravi: oncall playbook: when fallback triggers >5% of requests for 10m, create pager to SRE and notify account owner. include automated ingress throttling.
jess: procurement needs example invoice row: baseline price, burst credit price (consumed), overage rate, one-time onboarding fee. can product produce a sample invoice template?
maya: i'll draft sample invoices for Tier A/B/C with numbers. also add a calculator snippet for sales.
ben: telemetry: emit metrics: tenant.baseline_usage, tenant.burst_usage, tenant.burst_remaining, tenant.fallback_count, plus sampling traces for routing decisions. attach tags commit_tier and commit_id.
sam: chaos tests: plan simulated surge that exceeds burst and verifies graceful fallback and billing markers. ops-bot: scheduled chaos run Friday 03:00 UTC.
ops-bot: canary deployment scheduled: dedicated-routing-v2 -> 5% traffic for pilot tenants tomorrow 14:00 UTC.
maya: launch checklist (proposed): 1) API + tenant migration in prod staging 2) Console panels + invoice examples 3) Autoscale + fallback tested via chaos 4) Pilot with 3 customers (one per tier) 5) Legal and finance approve pricing docs 6) Run canary and SLO verification 7) GA.
lina: add a short customer SLA appendix describing p95 targets by tier and model-family caveats. procurement will ask.
ben: SLO draft: Tier small p95 < 250ms, Tier medium p95 < 180ms, Tier large p95 < 120ms (model-family exceptions documented). enforce via alerting.
ravi: operational note: prewarm window should be capped (max 4 hours) and rate-limited across DCs, otherwise noisy customers will starve prewarms.
jess: i'll recruit pilots and collect procurement constraints. need clear one-pager and demo script.
maya: thanks all. I'll author the RFC tonight: commit ladder definition, API contracts, billing examples, telemetry spec, oncall playbook, and chaos scenarios. please react with :thumbsup: if you're ok for me to proceed.
ben: :thumbsup:
